photo.title: A man, Engulé, with a tall spear standing behind an earth or termite mound. The mound may even have been shaped by elephants using their tusks. A large blade being held is also visible in the bottom right hand corner of the frame.
View along a wide river in a bai (natural clearing in the forest). A white bird, an egret, is just visible at the base of a tree in the middle rear of the image.

A large black millipede (ngongolo) crawling over a hardback book placed on the ground. The book is the Collins Field Guide to the Birds of West Africa by W Serle, G.J Morel and W. Hartwig (London, 1977). This image is related to image 1997.21.3.553.
View looking out from inside a dome-shaped shelter.
View of a stream the middle of the forest, probably at Boungingi).
View of trees through forest vegetation.

View looking up through forest vegetation towards the canopy. An unidentified man is visible on a branch high up engaged in an activity, probably going to gather honey. This image is related to image 1997.21.3.572.

View of a girl and another person sat outside a dome-shaped shelter in a clearing in the forest. The girl to the left is Bonolo. A large basket and tall spear are visible outside the shelter. In the mid-ground a girl is walking carrying a bag and some material on her back. This image is taken from inside a shelter and the left edge is very dark. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.579.

View of a girl,  Bonolo, and another person sat outside a dome-shaped shelter in a clearing in the forest. A large basket and tall spear are visible outside the shelter. This image is taken from inside a shelter and the edges are very dark. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.578.
View of a river flowing through the bai (natural clearing in the forest). Dense forest vegetation is visible at the edges and in the background.
View across the bai (natural clearing in the forest). Dense forest vegetation is visible in the background.
View of Boungingi bai, a natural clearing in the forest.
View of Boungingi bai, a natural clearing in the forest.

Three women walking through a path in the forest from camp towards a natural clearing to fetch water.. More people are just visible further ahead in the clearing. Dense forest vegetation is visible in the background at the far end of the clearing.
View along an elephant trail through the forest vegetation. The BayAka sometimes refer to these as bambango ('roads').
A large bird, possibly an ibis, flying above the treetops of the forest canopy.

A large gathering of women and children underneath a shelter made from logs with a thatched roof and open sides. Most of the group are facing forward and looking in the same direction towards someone or something out of frame to the left of the image. In the left hand side of the image a woman wearing a dress of printed material is standing up and is speaking. In the background there are buildings made from wooden logs and mud with thatched roofs. According to Louis Sarno, the women are probably acting out a story with mime. Named individuals include: Mbongi, Mafiki, Esusi, Mbina, Sepi and others. The women only gather here when there are no men present. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.612-614 and 1997.21.3.615.

Seven men and youths sat on the ground outside a building made of wooden poles and mud with a thatched roof. The youth second from the left is playing a geedal, or bow harp, a seven-stringed musical instrument, and is using both hands to pluck the strings. The instrument consists of a sound box, in one end of which is inserted a curved stick that projects outwards and upwards. On this stick are attached seven tuning pegs. A string is strung from each peg and attached to the sound box. The youth second from the right is sitting on a carved  upturned vessel that is goblet shaped.

None of the people named here are still alive [NJL 02/04/2012]
A small aircraft in the sky above the treetops of the forest. In the foreground there are two buildings made of wooden poles and mud with sloping thatched roofs. A view of rooftops at Kenyé.

View across the clearing of settlement looking towards a large group of people sitting underneath a shelter made of wooden poles with a roof and open sides. One woman is standing on her own in the clearing to the left of the shelter and appears to be addressing a smaller group sat outside the shelter in the right of the image. A large basket and a metal vessel lies on the floor in the right of the image. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.626.

Two types of shelter are visible: large structures made of wooden poles with sloping roofs, some of which are only partly completed, and also dome-shaped shelters covered in fronds. A dog is lying on the ground outside the building at the left of the image and a few other people are visible in the background. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.638.

A group of men and boys gathering wood and looking into vegetation, probably looking for a snake. The man at the front is breaking a long piece of wood into smaller pieces. In the foreground there is a small circular enclosed structure made of upright branches placed in the ground.

Group of mainly women and children standing and sitting outside the buildings of a settlement. Many of the women and children are wearing cloth with printed designs. Two types of shelter are visible: large structures made of wooden poles with sloping roofs, some of which are only partly completed, and also dome-shaped shelters covered in fronds.
Two men with spears and also a woman searching in the vegetation, probably for a snake, at the edge of a settlement. A small basket, smoke from a fire, and the edges of some shelters are visible.
Four men hunting in the vegetation. Two of the men have spears and one is wearing a headband. They are probably looking for a snake.
Four men hunting in the vegetation. Two of the men have spears and one is wearing a headband. Engbeté, one of Bombé's sons, is closest to the camera.

Mowanja building a mondumé (harp zither), a musical instrument. The man holds one end of a long stick in his mouth and a string is stretched the length of the stick and passes through a notch of a wooden bridge that is wedged in the stick  and raises the string above the stick. The man appears to be about the fix another string in place. Some wood shavings and a large blade lie on the ground in the foreground. Behind the man three people and a child are sitting outside a dome-shaped shelter.

Kulu building a mondumé (harp zither), a musical instrument. The instrument consists of long stick with a wooden bridge wedged into the stick approximately half way along. Three strings are stretched the length of the stick and are raised into different positions as they pass over different notches on the bridge. In the background two other men, a dome-shaped shelter and a metal vessel and large basket are visible. Kulu is Mowanja's son-in-law.

Makuti sat on the ground carving a cross bow. He is holding a long thin length of wood that has been carved with a box-shaped structure at the end that is closest to the ground. A pile of thin sticks lie close by. In the background a woman and some youths sit inside two different shelters. The crossbow is mainly used to hunt monkeys. This image is related to image 1997.21.3.657.

A woman, Ngbali, wife of Bombé, is sat on a raised wooden platform outside a dome-shaped shelter weaving a basket. A partly woven basket is visible leaning up against the outside of another shelter towards the centre of the frame. In the right of the frame three children are sat together on the ground and different types of vessel lie near them, including a carved wooden goblet-shaped vessel. The shelters are made from branches that are bent into arcs to form a framework that is covered with leaves.

A youth in the forest sat on top of a type of structure made of earth, or  fallen tree. The youth is building something or collecting material, and a wooden ladder is just visible in the bottom right of the image. This image is related to images 1997.21.3.668-669.

A child, Mekita, stood outside two dome-shaped shelters in the forest and looking at the camera. The shelters are made from branches that are bent into arcs to form a framework that is covered with leaves. A large woven basket is lying on the roof of the shelter on the left and a large metal vessel is visible between the shelters. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.670.

Domestic scene outside some dome-shaped shelters at the edge of a clearing in the forest. In the bottom left of the image a woman is sat on the ground weaving a large basket. Six children are stood together in a group in the centre close to some mats or other material. The shelters are made from branches that are bent into arcs to form a framework that is covered with leaves. Just behind the shelters in the left of the image some clothing hangs on a line. Kazinaw is fourth from the left in the beam of light.
Louis Sarno, four men and two children sat together underneath a shelter. Some of the group are sitting on a raised platform made of wooden logs. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.679.
View looking up through the forest canopy towards the sky above. The film has been damaged so the image is of low quality.

Three children outside a dome-shaped shelter. The child in the centre is holding the smallest child on his or her back. The shelter is made from branches that are bent into arcs to form a framework that is covered with leaves. In the background some clothes are hanging on a line behind the shelters.
Louis Sarno sat under a shelter with another man and a youth. The image is very dark and it is difficult to pick out clear details.
Very dark image - no clear details to decribe.

Two people sat outside a wooden structure made of logs in a settlement in the forest. A small fire is visible and some clothes are hanging on a line in the background. The image is dark and it is difficult to see clear details.
Image of forest vegetation. The image is blurred and it is difficult to see clear details.
View looking through forest vegetation towards the sky above the canopy. This image is similar to images 1997.21.3.717-718.
Close-up of fallen white blossoms on top of leaves on the forest floor. The image is slightly out of focus and so the details are unclear. The image is similar to image 1997.21.725.

Two women with baskets bags walking through the forest, probably while moving camp The woman on the left is carrying the bag or basket on her head and the woman on the right has a mortar (kingili) on her back held by a strap across her forehead. Louis thinks this may be heading towards Likumbi (another river).
View looking up a tree trunk in the forest towards the forest canopy and the sky above.
View of tree in the forest looking towards the forest canopy and the sky above.
Close-up of the base of a tree trunk in the forest. The trunk appears to be partly rotting. This image is related to images 1997.21.3.742 and 1997.21.3.744
View looking up the trunk of a large tree towards the forest canopy and the sky above. Lianas are railing up and down the trunk. This image is similar to images 1997.21.3.746-747.

View looking up the trunk of a large tree towards the forest canopy and the sky above. Lianas are trailing up and down the trunk. This image is similar to images 1997.21.3.745 and image 1997.21.3.747.

View of forest vegetation including palm trees with narrow fronds. In the centre of the frame there is a cluster of fruits supported by the branches of a tree. This image is similar to images 1997.21.3.751-752.

A youth climbing up the trailing vines of a tree in the forest. A spear is visible leaning against a tree trunk on the left side of the frame. The head of another person is just visible at the bottom left of the frame. This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.754.
View of palm trees and other plants and trees in the forest vegetation with sky visible in the background.
A hunting net strung between trees and vegetation. Hunting nets are called makya (singular: bokya). This image is similar to image 1997.21.3.764.

The buildings and shelters in a settlement at the edge of a clearing in the forest. Two types of shelter are visible: large structures made of wooden poles and mud with sloping thatched roofs, and also dome-shaped shelters made from branches covered in fronds. In the foreground the framework for a dome-shaped shelter that has not yet been covered in leaves is visible. Baskets and metal vessels are scattered on the ground and in the background somebody is crouching on the ground engaged in activity outside a building.

A man, Engulé, pulling back the wire of a crossbow with a group of women standing just behind him in the forest. A spear is visible at the right edge of the frame. The women are wearing brightly designed printed cloth. The woman on the left is wearing a necklace. The woman in the centre is wearing dangly earrings and the woman to the right is wearing a headscarf.
A child, Mekita,  wearing a beige cloth cap looking at the camera. More people are visible in the background but are out of focus.

A youth, Pumbwa, sat on the forest floor looking at the camera. In front of the child there is a collected pile of leaves and two rolled up plastic mats. Another child is sitting on the left and is wrapping a pile of sticks together. A wooden axe lies on the floor next to Pumbwa.

An unidentified man sat under a dome-shaped shelter in the forest. The shelter is made from branches that are bent into arcs to form a framework that is covered with leaves. A tall spear is leaning up against the outside of the shelter and another shelter is visible in the left of the frame.

A woman, girls and children outside some dome-shaped settlements in a clearing in the forest. The woman farthest on the left is carrying a baby in a sling on her shoulder and two baskets are visible lying outside the shelters.
Femme Babinga frappant une cloche de fer
